# Spenser

> A chocolate dispenser that speaks FHIR R5. It treats chocolate as a
> medication: you place a MedicationRequest, it dispenses a piece and reports a
> MedicationDispense. It is both a FHIR server, for orders posted straight at
> it, and a FHIR client, polling an order server for orders it should fulfil.

This file is written for AI agents and for people using them. It is served by
the device itself, so whatever you are reading describes THIS unit. Fetch it
from http://spenser.local/llms.txt, or from <this unit's address>/llms.txt.

Use it to write examples, tests and client code without guessing. Every shape
below is what the firmware actually accepts or produces. When something here
disagrees with the device, the device is right: check GET /metadata, which is
the CapabilityStatement this unit publishes.

Specification and examples: http://costateixeira.github.io/spenser


## The key

Reads are open. Everything that changes this unit needs its key: dispensing,
settings, Wi-Fi, inventory, updates. Without it those routes answer 401 with an
OperationOutcome.

Send it any of three ways:

    Authorization: Bearer <key>
    X-Spenser-Key: <key>
    ?key=<key>

The key is 32 hex characters, generated on the unit's first boot and printed on
its serial console at every boot. GET /key returns it for five minutes after a
restart, and at any time while the unit is in setup mode, which is the window
its owner has and nobody else does. After that window, restart the unit or read
the console.

A unit in setup mode, serving its own access point, accepts everything without
a key: there is no network to defend and whoever is standing next to it has
already won.


## The one thing to understand first

A FHIR request is an authorization, not an instruction. Spenser will not
dispense just because an order exists. An order becomes actionable in one of
two ways, per the HL7 Clinical Orders Workflow guidance:

1. A tag: the MedicationRequest carries meta.tag
   http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/common-tags#actionable
2. A Task: a Task with status "requested" points at the order in Task.focus

These are not two modes of the device. It looks for both on every check and
acts on whichever turns up. When an order arrives by both routes at once the
Task wins, and the order is still dispensed exactly once. The orderMode
setting narrows it to one route, which is only useful for demonstrating the
difference.

Who closes the order differs, and this trips people up:

- No Task involved: Spenser sets the MedicationRequest to "completed" itself.
- A Task involved: Spenser sets the Task to "completed" and puts the dispense
  in Task.output. The MedicationRequest is left "active", because closing the
  request is the placer's job, not the filler's.


## What it can dispense

Two codes, from the system
http://costateixeira.github.io/spenser/CodeSystem/SpenserMeds

- chocolate-dark  "Dark Chocolate"
- chocolate-milk  "Milk Chocolate"

One piece per order. Each lane has its own count, and an order for an empty
lane is declined rather than queued. R5 puts the medication in
medication.concept, not the R4 medicationCodeableConcept, although this unit
still accepts the R4 spelling on a directly posted order.


## FHIR interface, served by this device

Errors are always an OperationOutcome with application/fhir+json. There is no
second error format.

GET /metadata
  CapabilityStatement. Declares both roles, the search parameters below, the
  $dispense operation, software.version, and how the key works.

POST /MedicationRequest                                  [key]
  A create that also dispenses, because posting an order at this unit is
  itself the decision to fill it.
  You do not need to supply an id; the unit assigns one when you leave it out.
  201 with a Location header pointing at the created order, an ETag, and the
  created MedicationRequest as the body.
  Prefer: return=minimal gives an empty body, Prefer: return=OperationOutcome
  gives a summary of what happened.
  The order is kept, so GET it back afterwards. What came out of the machine is
  a separate resource at /MedicationDispense/{id}-dispense, or
  /MedicationDispense/{id}-declined when the lane was empty.
  400 with an OperationOutcome when the body is not a usable order.

POST /$dispense                                          [key]
  The one-call path, and the one to use when what you want back is the
  dispense. Body is a MedicationRequest, or Parameters carrying one.
  200 with the MedicationDispense, completed or declined. An operation reports
  itself in the resource it returns, so an empty lane is still a 200.
  Also answers at /MedicationRequest/$dispense.

GET /MedicationRequest
GET /MedicationRequest/{id}
  The orders posted to this unit, which it keeps. Searchable by _id, status,
  subject and _count. Orders it polled from a server are not here: they live on
  that server.

GET /MedicationDispense
GET /MedicationDispense/{id}
  What this unit dispensed or refused to dispense, newest first, from polled
  orders and direct posts alike. Searchable by _id, status, subject,
  authorizingPrescription and _count, where a reference matches either in full
  or by id alone, so subject=Patient/123 and subject=123 both work.
  The searchset also carries an OperationOutcome entry with search.mode
  "outcome" describing the last check of the order server: severity
  information, warning or error, the message in issue.diagnostics, and the
  server, accepted routes, age and counts in issue.details.text. Read that
  entry to find out what the device is doing.
  Both stores live on the unit's filesystem, so a restart or an update does not
  erase them. The oldest records are dropped when a store fills.

GET /InventoryReport
  Current stock as an InventoryReport, one inventoryListing per lane.
  reportedDateTime is the real time when the unit has a clock.

POST /InventoryReport                                    [key]
  Set stock from a report. countType "snapshot" sets the count, "difference"
  adds to it. Stock is persisted, so it survives a restart.


## What this device asks of an order server

Set the server with GET /setSettings?serverUrl=... Then, on every check, it
runs two searches and writes back what happened.

  GET  {server}/Task?status=requested&_include=Task:focus&_count=5
  GET  {server}/MedicationRequest?_tag=http%3A%2F%2Fterminology.hl7.org%2FCodeSystem%2Fcommon-tags%7Cactionable&status=active&intent=instance-order&_count=5
  POST {server}/MedicationDispense
  PUT  {server}/Task/{id}                 (completed, or failed when it gives up)
  PUT  {server}/MedicationRequest/{id}    (completed, only when no Task is involved)

The _include matters: the device resolves Task.focus from the entries in that
one Bundle rather than fetching each order separately. A Task whose focus is
not in the Bundle is reported as a problem and skipped.

_count=5 matters when you are testing: only the first five results of each
search are considered per check, so with a longer queue a specific order may
not be picked up on a given check.

Both http:// and https:// work. Certificates are not validated.


## Time

A dispense carries recorded, whenPrepared and whenHandedOver, and a refusal
carries recorded, as soon as the unit has reached an NTP server. Until then
those elements are left out rather than guessed, so an absent timestamp means
"this unit had no clock", never "this happened at the epoch". GET /ota/status
reports the clock.


## Updates, over the air

The firmware and these web files are both replaceable over Wi-Fi. The chip
keeps two application slots; an upload goes into the one that is not running
and the unit reboots into it.

GET /ota/status
  Version, build, which slot is running, how much of it the image uses, whether
  a rollback is possible, the manifest URL, the clock, and the last result.

POST /ota/firmware                                       [key]
  Body is firmware.bin itself, not a form. The unit restarts on success.

POST /ota/filesystem                                     [key]
  Body is spiffs.bin, the image holding these web files. The unit restarts.

POST /ota/file?path=/index.html                          [key]
  Body is one file, written to that path. No restart, nothing rebuilt. This is
  the one to use while iterating on the dashboard or on this guide.

POST /ota/check                                          [key]
  Fetch the manifest at updateUrl and install it when its version differs from
  this unit's. Returns 202: like a check for orders, the work happens in the
  main loop.

POST /ota/rollback                                       [key]
  Go back to the previous image and restart.

A release manifest looks like this, and a unit set to check it keeps itself up
to date:

    { "version": "1.2.0",
      "firmware": "https://.../firmware.bin",
      "filesystem": "https://.../spiffs.bin" }

    GET /setSettings?updateUrl=https://.../manifest.json&updateCheckHours=24

A new image is marked good only after it has been up a minute with a network,
so a build that cannot get that far leaves the previous one in place.


## Non-FHIR interface, this unit's own admin API

Everything here is JSON or plain text, and none of it is FHIR. It exists to
configure and drive the unit, not to exchange clinical data. Everything that
changes something needs the key.

Orders
  GET /checkOrders        Ask for a check now. Returns 202 immediately: the
                          HTTP work happens in the main loop, not while
                          answering this request. Give it a few seconds, or
                          poll GET /MedicationDispense until the outcome entry
                          stops saying a check is in progress.
  GET /orders             The last check as plain JSON, for the dashboard:
                          mode, serverUrl, busy, everRan, secondsAgo,
                          httpStatus, found, dispensed, message, handled,
                          queuedRetries.
  GET /forgetOrders       Forget which orders were already dealt with, so the
                          same order can be dispensed again. Useful between
                          test runs.

Settings
  GET /settings           Everything stored in NVS.
  GET /setSettings?...    Any of: serverUrl, orderMode (both, tag or task),
                          orderQuery, taskQuery, pollEnabled (0 or 1),
                          pollSeconds (5 to 3600), writeBack (0 or 1),
                          giveUpOnStockEmpty (0 or 1), updateUrl,
                          updateCheckHours, servoDark, servoMilk, angleRest,
                          anglePush, returnDelayMs. Answers with the full
                          settings JSON, which includes firmwareVersion and
                          never includes the key. 400 when nothing is known.
  GET /resetSettings      Back to the compiled-in defaults.

Stock and hardware
  GET /inventory          Plain counts.
  GET /setInventory?dark=&milk=
  GET /resetInventory?dark=&milk=
  GET /setServos?dark=&milk=
  GET /flashServo1, /flashServo2
  GET /setColor?r=&g=&b=
  GET /battery            Voltage, current, percent, and whether it is on USB,
                          charging or running off the pack.
  GET /reset              Reboot.

Wi-Fi and identity
  GET /, /scan, /cfg, POST /save, /wifi-settings, /wifi-reset,
  /wifi-reboot-config, /getMac, /setMac, /clearMac
  GET /key               This unit's key, during the window described above.

Captive portal
  /generate_204, /hotspot-detect.html, /fwlink, /ncsi.txt, /connecttest.txt

Anything else falls back to a static file from the device filesystem, which is
how the dashboard at / is served. OPTIONS returns 200 for CORS preflight.

Not HTTP at all: it advertises itself over mDNS as spenser, serves an open
access point with a captive portal when it has no Wi-Fi, logs to serial at
115200 baud, and has a button. A short press dispenses, three seconds is a
soft reset, ten seconds wipes the stored credentials.


## Polling

By default it checks every 30 seconds while pollEnabled is on. The interval is
pollSeconds, clamped between 5 and 3600. /checkOrders forces one immediately.

When you are writing tests, turn polling off with
GET /setSettings?pollEnabled=0 so that only your explicit checks run.
Otherwise a background poll can fulfil an order before your test looks, and
your assertions will race.


## Examples you can copy

An order made actionable by a tag. Place this on the order server, not on the
device. Spenser will dispense it and set it to completed.

    {
      "resourceType": "MedicationRequest",
      "meta": {
        "tag": [
          { "system": "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/common-tags",
            "code": "actionable" }
        ]
      },
      "status": "active",
      "intent": "instance-order",
      "medication": {
        "concept": {
          "coding": [
            { "system": "http://costateixeira.github.io/spenser/CodeSystem/SpenserMeds",
              "code": "chocolate-dark",
              "display": "Dark Chocolate" }
          ]
        }
      },
      "subject": { "reference": "Patient/123" },
      "dosageInstruction": [ { "text": "One bite" } ]
    }

The same order without the tag is ignored. That is the negative test: place it,
ask for a check, and assert that nothing was dispensed and the order is still
active.

A Task that makes a plain order actionable. Post the order first, then this,
with its real id in focus.

    {
      "resourceType": "Task",
      "identifier": [
        { "system": "http://example.org/spenser-orders", "value": "demo-1" }
      ],
      "status": "requested",
      "intent": "order",
      "code": {
        "coding": [
          { "system": "http://hl7.org/fhir/CodeSystem/task-code",
            "code": "fulfill" }
        ]
      },
      "focus": { "reference": "MedicationRequest/<the order id>" },
      "for": { "reference": "Patient/123" }
    }

An order posted straight at the device, which dispenses on the spot. This is
the operation, so the answer is the MedicationDispense itself:

    curl -X POST http://spenser.local/\$dispense \
      -H "Content-Type: application/fhir+json" \
      -H "X-Spenser-Key: $KEY" \
      -d '{"resourceType":"MedicationRequest","id":"demo-direct",
           "status":"active","intent":"instance-order",
           "medication":{"concept":{"coding":[
             {"system":"http://costateixeira.github.io/spenser/CodeSystem/SpenserMeds",
              "code":"chocolate-milk","display":"Milk Chocolate"}]}},
           "subject":{"reference":"Patient/123"}}'

It answers with the MedicationDispense, and you can read it back afterwards at
GET /MedicationDispense/demo-direct-dispense. POST the same body to
/MedicationRequest instead and you get a 201 with a Location, the created order
as the body, and the dispense waiting at that same place.

What a refusal looks like. R5 removed MedicationDispense.statusReason, so the
reason lives in notPerformedReason, which is a CodeableReference, hence the
.concept in the path:

    {
      "resourceType": "MedicationDispense",
      "id": "<order id>-declined",
      "status": "declined",
      "notPerformedReason": {
        "concept": {
          "coding": [
            { "system": "http://hl7.org/fhir/CodeSystem/medicationdispense-status-reason",
              "code": "outofstock",
              "display": "Drug not available - out of stock" }
          ]
        }
      },
      "medication": { "concept": { "coding": [ { "code": "chocolate-dark" } ] } },
      "subject": { "reference": "Patient/123" },
      "authorizingPrescription": [ { "reference": "MedicationRequest/<order id>" } ]
    }


## A test that exercises the whole loop

    # 0. the key, once: read it from the serial console, or within five
    #    minutes of a restart
    KEY=$(curl -s http://spenser.local/key | sed -n 's/.*"key":"\([a-f0-9]*\)".*/\1/p')
    AUTH="-H \"X-Spenser-Key: $KEY\""

    # 1. a known state: both routes accepted, stock in both lanes, no polling
    curl -H "X-Spenser-Key: $KEY" "http://spenser.local/setSettings?serverUrl=$SERVER&orderMode=both&writeBack=1&pollEnabled=0&giveUpOnStockEmpty=0"
    curl -H "X-Spenser-Key: $KEY" "http://spenser.local/resetInventory?dark=10&milk=10"
    curl -H "X-Spenser-Key: $KEY" "http://spenser.local/forgetOrders"

    # 2. place an actionable order on the server, keep its id
    curl -X POST "$SERVER/MedicationRequest" -H "Content-Type: application/fhir+json" -d @order.json

    # 3. ask for a check, then wait for it to finish
    curl -H "X-Spenser-Key: $KEY" "http://spenser.local/checkOrders"

    # 4. what the device did, and whether the check itself was clean
    curl -H "Accept: application/fhir+json" "http://spenser.local/MedicationDispense"

    # 5. the server's side of the story
    curl "$SERVER/MedicationRequest/<id>"        # completed
    curl "$SERVER/MedicationDispense?_count=20"  # a dispense pointing back at it

Assert on the FHIR, not on the prose: the dispense status, the
authorizingPrescription reference, the order status, and for the out of stock
case notPerformedReason.concept.coding.code. The OperationOutcome severity
tells you whether the check itself went wrong, which is a different failure
from an order that was correctly left alone.


## Things that will catch you out

- Nothing happens and the order stays active: it is probably not actionable.
  No tag, no Task, or the Task is not "requested".
- The device dispensed once and then ignores the same order: it remembers what
  it has handled. GET /forgetOrders clears that.
- An out of stock order is reported once, not on every poll. With
  giveUpOnStockEmpty=0 it stays open and goes through after a refill. With =1
  it is abandoned, and in that case a coordinating Task is set to "failed".
- /checkOrders returns 202 before any work is done. Assert after the check has
  finished, not after a fixed sleep.
- A search that returns a chunked response is fine, but anything the device
  cannot parse shows up as a Bundle error in the outcome entry rather than as
  a failed HTTP status.
- Placing an order with an unresolved template variable leaves a Task pointing
  at nothing. The device will report it and move on, and it will sit on the
  server forever.
- A 401 is about the key, not the body. Reads never need it, writes always do.
- A create answers 201 and returns the order, not the dispense. Use /$dispense
  when you want the dispense in one call.
- An absent timestamp means the unit has no clock yet, not that the event had
  no time. The clock is reported in /ota/status.
- An update reboots the unit. Stock, the dispense record and the order record
  all survive it. A check in progress does not, and an upload is refused while
  one is running.
